units.translation: b. Like a maiden: he has made the comparison incongruously; for he supposes Jason to be an old woman and his mother a maiden; but they say it should have been arranged in the opposite way. But we shall say that Jason is appropriately placed not according to age, but according to the care of his mother—for the old woman rears the maiden—, as the mother is suited both to helplessness because of age—for old age and tender age are alike—and to needing someone to nourish her. And Pelias lies upon them like a harsh stepmother. And κηδεμονῆες is derived from κηδε-

f. 〈ἡ οὐκ εἰσὶν ἔτ’ ἄλλοι:〉 this also refers to Alcimede, who has no other children. Lm

g. 〈ὑπὸ μητρυιῇ〉 βίοτον βαρὺν 〈ἡγηλάζει〉: the word οὖσα is missing; being under a stepmother she leads a wretched life. For βίοτος is used both of life, as here, and of wealth. And ἡγηλάζει and ἠλάσκει are used of the same thing; they mean to spend time in the same place and to be entangled and to move about in the same place. For Homer says of flies (Iliad 2.470): 'which buzz about the pastoral steading' and (Odyssey 9.457): 'wherever that one wanders with my strength'.

b. 〈ἐστυφέλιξεν:〉 instead of attacked, grieved. Lg

275 a. ἐκφλύξαι: instead of to say. And properly we say that boiling cauldrons φλύζειν, that is, throw up water with heat. And ὀρεχθεῖν is circumflexed like ποιεῖν; it is an imitation of an inarticulate sound. Homer (Iliad 23.30): 'many oxen bellowed'. But it should rather be understood as groaning.
b. 〈ὀρεχθεῖ:〉 is distressed. And Homer (Odyssey 5.83): 'groaning in his heart with grief'. Lm(P)
